newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian OLOs to watch politics, franc for now.
newsitem.headline: Belgian OLOs to watch politics, franc for now.

text.p: The Belgian OLO market was expected to open nervously again on Monday after so far having weathered a domestic political crisis that has driven the Belgian franc lower against the mark.

OLOs ended higher on Friday, helped by a rise in Bunds on the back of a raft of U.S. data. The yield on the benchmark March 2007 OLO fell to 5.81 percent from 5.85 percent, while the spread over Bunds was little changed.
The franc failed to get a boost, however, remaining at low levels hit on Thursday following fresh twists in a bribes scandal that has engulfed a government coaltion party.
"The scandal has people sidelined and sidelined means no sellers," one OLO trader said. "The currency is a little bit weak, but we don't see anything on the OLO side which is strange."

He said the direction of the market on Monday would depend on what new facts, if any, in the bribes scandal emerged over the weekend. Volumes would remain low ahead of a meeting of the U.S. Federal Reserve's policy making Federal Open Market Committee on Tuesday, and with a G-7 finance ministers gathering at the end of the week. "But I don't expect sellers. They would have done it by now," he added.

The Belgian franc was quoted at 20.6293/03 to the mark on Friday, off lows around 20.6380/00 and up from 20.6330/50 late on Thursday. March Bibor contracts ended down 0.01 at 96.85, off a low of 96.82.
"I expect the currency to come back to around 20.61/62," one trader said.
